newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels claim three more towns on way to Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Rebels claim three more towns on way to Kinshasa.

text.p: Zaire's rebel forces announced on Wednesday the capture of three towns east of the capital Kinshasa and said they were closing in on the last redoubt of President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"We can announce tonight the capture of Bowete, Tshikapa and Ilebo," rebel "justice minister" Kongolo Mwenge told a news conference, naming towns around 200 km east of Kikwit on the main highway to Kinshasa.
"We are also approaching Kikwit and our progress is going on normally," he added.
He said he could not immediately confirm reports that rebel forces had also taken Boma, a coastal town to the west of Kinshasa.

Asked if rebel forces planned to attack Kinshasa from the southwest, entering Zaire from Angolan territory, the official said: "The Angolans are our friends, that's for sure. But our troops are not in Angola."
Mwenge said he believed the fall of Kinshasa was a "matter of days rather than weeks" and added that in his personal opinion there would not be a bloody battle for the capital.

At the news conference in Lubumbashi, Laurent Kabila's rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) paraded a general and five colonels of the defeated Zaire army, the FAZ.

A general called Molambo, who described himself as chief of the First Military District of Shaba province, said the AFDL forces were militarily very strong and appealed to some of his men still hiding in the bush or in the city itself to give themselves up without fear of abuse.
"We gave ourselves up freely. We were welcomed warmly and fed and lodged," he said. The officers were dressed in civilian clothes and appeared to be in normal physical condition.
Molambo revealed that he had hidden "in the bush" for 10 days before giving himself up to a Roman Catholic priest.

"I can attest that other soldiers are in the bush. I appeal to them to give themselves up, come in and work together for the Alliance. We have seen there have been abuses (under the Mobutu regime). The Alliance has good ideas," he said.
The other captured officers were named as Colonels Ononga, Mambo, Longelo, Kosanga and Akambo.

Colonel Ononga, who said he was trained at France's Saint Cyr military academy, was applauded by local people attending the display when he said: "We ask pardon of the people of Katanga (the previous name of Shaba province)."

According to the AFDL, which has made Lubumbashi its headquarters until it captures Kinshasa, there were still some government troops in hiding in the area. "We still have some soldiers in the city who haven't given up yet," Mwenge said.

Aides to Kabila, who has remained in seclusion virtually since he arrived in Zaire's second city following its capture two weeks ago, have spoken of threats to the life of their leader, but have given no details.
